enrichment.headline: Approves up to $169,356.95 for Titan nutrition program software through June 2021
enrichment.summary: The district is buying Titan School Solutions software to manage the student nutrition program. The cost is capped at $169,356.95 over the whole term, with yearly limits of $62,378.00 for November 2019 to June 2020 and $106,978.95 for 2020-21. It runs from November 14, 2019 through June 30, 2021, and is managed by the Nutrition Services Department.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Titan School Solutions - Nutrition Program Management Software - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Hires Hazelrigg to adjust workers' compensation claims, up to $2,090,772 over three years
enrichment.summary: The district is hiring Hazelrigg Claims Management Service, an outside claims administrator, to handle workers' compensation claims. The total is capped at $2,090,772.00 for July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023, with yearly limits of $669,760.00, $696,550.00 and $724,412.00. The contract also has two one-year renewal options and is paid from the district's self-insurance fund.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Contract – District and Hazelrigg Claims Management Service - Workers’ Compensations Claims - Risk Management Department

enrichment.headline: Moves $250,000 milk and dairy bid from closed Berkeley Farms to Crystal Creamery
enrichment.summary: Berkeley Farms Dairy stopped doing business, so the district is moving its milk and dairy bid award to Crystal Creamery, the second-lowest responsive and responsible bidder. The amount is capped at $250,000.00 for the rest of the 2019-20 school year, with two one-year renewal options. The Superintendent already took this action, and the Board is being asked to ratify it.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Transfer - Award of Bid - Milk/Dairy Products - RFP/Bid No. 19-01 - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts $97,500 from No Kid Hungry for grab-and-go meals during COVID-19
enrichment.summary: The district is accepting a $97,500.00 grant from the No Kid Hungry Campaign.
